texts.preamble: Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Kabc020223602021 Before The Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Bangalore. (Scch-9) Dated This The 19th Day Of November 2025 Present Smt.Nirmala.M.C.,B.Com.,L.L.B ., Judge, Court Of Small Causes & Acjm Mvc No.3623/2021
texts.facts: Due to impact petitioner and his pillion riders were thrown out from the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries. Immediately after the accident, petitioner was shifted to Govt., General Hospital, Gowribidanur wherein first aid was done, then he was shifted to Someshwara hospital, Gowribidanur wherein the petitioner was treated as inpatient and underwent wound debridement. Prior to the accident, petitioner was Agriculturist, Sericulturist and doing milk vending work and earning (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.3623/2021 monthly Rs.20,000/- per month. Due to said accident, he lost his future income. The Gowribidanur rural police have registered a criminal case against the driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 in crime No.0207/2020 under Section 279, 337 and 304A of IPC. The respondent No.2 being the RC owner and respondent No.1 being the insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner. 3. After service of summons, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the court hence, placed exparte and respondent No.1 has appeared before the tribunal and filed its written statement. 4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.1 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts. It has admitted the issuance of the policy in favour of the respondent No.2. Respondent No.1 has denied the involvement of the car bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-9275 in the alleged accident. It (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.3623/2021 has denied the age, occupation, income and amount spent by the petitioner. Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending vehicle regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/ 2 required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6) of MV Act. It has contented that, at the time of accident, petitioner was not wearing safety headgear which is clear violation of MV Act. There are three persons are traveling on the motor cycle against to its seating capacity and lost control over the same and caused the accident. The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, exorbitant and exaggerated. With these grounds the respondent No.1 sought for rejecting the claim petition. 5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues: (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.3623/2021 ISSUES 1. In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1, One Dr.Nagaraj B.N. at Sai Ortho and Dental Center as PW.2 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13. The respondent No.1 got examined one V.Nagaraj Achar -RTO-Chikkaballapura as RW-1 and got marked Ex-R1. (SCCH-9) 7 MVC.No.3623/2021 7. Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record. 8. My answer to the above issues are as under:- Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative; Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following: Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/ 3 -:R E A S O N S:- 9. Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 13.08.2020 at about 5.30 pm., when he was riding the TVS Heavy Duty Moped bearing reg.No.KA-50-K-3655 along with his mother Smt.Gangamma and his 4 year son Lokesh Babu as his pillion riders on the left side of gudibande-Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, Gowribidanur road, near Lakkasandra gate, driver of the car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner without following traffic rules and regulations, all of a sudden came from back side and (SCCH-9) 8 MVC.No.3623/2021 dashed against the petitioner's moped from behind. Due to impact petitioner and his pillion riders were thrown out form the moped and sustained severe head and bodily injuries. 10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition. He also got marked Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13 which are FIR, statement, mahazar, wound certificate, IMV report, charge sheet, discharge summary , adhar card, medical bills statements. 11. On perusal of police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P6 it is clear that the accident took place on 13-08-2020 at about 5.30 p.m., and Ex.P.1 - FIR in crime No.0207/2020 came to be registered on 13-08- 2020 i.e., on the same of accident at Gowribidanur Police Station for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337, 304A of IPC. Ex.P.2 - complaint lodged by petitioner on 13-08- (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.3623/2021 2020. Ex.P.3 is the panchanama, Ex.P4 is the woud certificate, Ex.P5 is the IMV report, Ex.P6 is the charge sheet which describe the spot of accident as towards Gowribidanur, Gudibande road, D palya cross, near Lakkasandra gate and Ex.P.7 is the discharge summary, Ex.P.5 is the IMV report which shows the damages caused the vehicles which involved in the alleged accident I.e., motor cycle bearing No.KA-50-K-3655 and car bearing No.KA-40-A-9275. Ex.P.6 is the charge sheet which has been filed against the driver of car bearing No.KA-40-A- 9275. 12. The learned counsel for the respondent No.1 has cross examined PW-1. I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1. The petitioner has contended due to accident he has sustained grievous injury i.e., tenderness over left pelvic region, tenderness over left shoulder, tenderness over chest and abdomen, cLW over right side of forehead 3 x 1 x 1 cms, CLW over back of head 10 x 2 x 2 cms, tenderness and swelling of left leg. In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P.4 issued by General Hospital, Gauribidanur which reveals that petitioner had sustained fibula fracture left leg and left scapular body fracture and doctor has opined that injury No.2 and 7 are grievous in nature and remaining injuries are simple in nature. Further, Petitioner examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N. and got marked clinical report and X-ray marked at Ex.P.12 and Ex.P.13.
texts.arguments: It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343. Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under: 14,500 x 12 x 14 x 8% = Rs.1,94,880/- Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.1,94,880/- under the head of loss of future earning capacity. Ramanjinappa vs Shri Ram Gen Ins Co Ltd on 19 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127453556/ 6 f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities: The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he cannot carryout his work/any manual work. PW.2 deposed that on examination petitioner complains of pain and weakness in the left shoulder, unable to lift weight sin the left arm and carry his routine work as before. At this juncture, this tribunal relied upon the decision reported in - MFA No.3459/2021(MV-1) ( Sri. Sadath Ali Khan Va. Sri. Noor Ahmed Sayeed and another) wherein it is held that - (SCCH-9) 20 MVC.No.3623/2021 " 26. Courts have consistently held that the compensation awarded should not be diluted solely because the injured party was not wearing protective headgear. The principle of "just compensation" requires that while contributory negligence can be a factor in determining the amount of compensation, it should not result in an unjust reduction.
